newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea agrees to peace talks if aid guaranteed.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea agrees to peace talks if aid guaranteed.

text.p: North Korea has told the United States and South Korea it will join proposed four-nation peace talks if they first offer guarantees of food aid, a Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
"North Korea made a formal response to the proposal for the four-nation talks in a working-level meeting in New York on Wednesday," Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters.

The talks, proposed jointly by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam last April, are aimed at forging a lasting peace mechanism to replace a truce agreement that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.

Wednesday's meeting was the first working-level contact since senior representatives from the United States and South Korea met North Korean diplomats for a briefing on the talks, which would also include China.
"We have repeated our position that food aid can be discussed in the four-party talks in the framework of easing tension and building peace," Lee said. "The United States maintains the same stand."
Seoul officials have said Pyongyang's interest in the peace talks reflected its desperation for food to stave off famine.
